task.title: Configuring the Ceph Ansible node (ceph05)
task.shortdesc: To deploy a Ceph cluster with Ansible, you can configure the ceph05 administration node, prepare inventory files, and run the ceph-ansible playbook against the monitor and OSD nodes.

context.p: Log into the Ceph Ansible node (ceph05) and configure it as follows. You will need the ceph01, ceph02, and ceph03 nodes to be running to complete these steps.

step.cmd: In the Ansible user’s home directory create a directory to store temporary values created from the ceph-ansible playbook

Enable password-less ssh for the ansible user. Run ssh-keygen on ceph05 (leave passphrase empty), then run and repeat ssh-copy-id to copy the public key to the Ansible user on ceph01, ceph02, and ceph03 systems:

info.codeblock: # USER_NAME=ansibleadmin # sudo su - $USER_NAME [ansibleadmin@ceph05 ~]$ ssh-keygen [ansibleadmin@ceph05 ~]$ ssh-copy-id $USER_NAME@ceph01 [ansibleadmin@ceph05 ~]$ ssh-copy-id $USER_NAME@ceph02 [ansibleadmin@ceph05 ~]$ ssh-copy-id $USER_NAME@ceph03 [ansibleadmin@ceph05 ~]$ exit #

step.cmd: Create a symbolic between these two directories:
Create copies of Ceph sample yml files to modify:

info.codeblock: # cd /usr/share/ceph-ansible # cp group_vars/all.yml.sample group_vars/all.yml # cp group_vars/osds.yml.sample group_vars/osds.yml # cp site.yml.sample site.yml

step.cmd: Edit the copied group_vars/all.yml file. See General Ansible Settings in Additional resources for details. For example:

info.codeblock: ceph_origin: repository ceph_repository: rhcs ceph_repository_type: cdn ceph_rhcs_version: 3 monitor_interface: eth0 public_network: 192.168.122.0/24
info.p: Note that your network device and address range may differ.

step.cmd: Edit the copied group_vars/osds.yml file. See the OSD Ansible Settings in Additional resources for details. In this example, the second disk device (/dev/sdb) on each OSD node is used for both data and journal storage:

info.codeblock: osd_scenario: collocated devices: - /dev/sdb dmcrypt: true osd_auto_discovery: false

step.cmd: Edit the /etc/ansible/hosts inventory file to identify the Ceph nodes as Ceph monitor, OSD and manager nodes. In this example, the storage devices are identified on each node as well:

info.codeblock:
[mons] ceph01 ceph02 ceph03
[osds] ceph01 devices="[ '/dev/sdb' ]" ceph02 devices="[ '/dev/sdb' ]" ceph03 devices="[ '/dev/sdb' ]"
[mgrs] ceph01 devices="[ '/dev/sdb' ]" ceph02 devices="[ '/dev/sdb' ]" ceph03 devices="[ '/dev/sdb' ]"

Run the ceph-ansible playbook (as your Ansible user):

info.p: At this point, the Ansible playbook checks your Ceph nodes and configures them for the services you requested. If anything fails, make needed corrections and rerun the command.

step.cmd: Log into one of the three Ceph nodes (ceph01, ceph02, or ceph03) and check the health of the Ceph cluster:
On the same node, verify that monitoring is working using rados:

info.codeblock: # ceph osd pool create test 8 # echo 'Hello World!' > hello-world.txt # rados --pool test put hello-world hello-world.txt # rados --pool test get hello-world fetch.txt # cat fetch.txt Hello World!
